lastWeekReview.title: Moses—The Ten Commandments (1)
bullets: God called Moses up Mount Sinai — with thunder, lightning, and a loud trumpet, everyone knew God was there!
God gave the Ten Commandments so His people would know how to live AND know what HE is really like.
1. No other gods    2. No idols    3. Don't misuse God's name
4. Remember the Sabbath    5. Honor your father and mother
The first five commandments are all about loving and honoring GOD first.
God's commandments are like a window into His heart!
lastWeekReview.discussion: Which of the first five commandments did you practice this week? What did it show you about God? Share your story!
lastWeekReview.verseQuote: "If you love Me, you will keep My commandments." — John 14:15

kidsContent.text: Last week we learned the FIRST five commandments — they are all about loving and honoring GOD.
This week we learn the LAST five commandments. These are about how we treat OTHER people!
God's laws aren't just a long to-do list. They are God speaking to us — showing us how His people should live.
Because we belong to God, like the children of Israel, we can learn to behave like God's people — in the small things AND the big things.
🌟 God gave us rules to show us how proper people should behave — and to make us more like Him!

image.caption: Moses gives God's words to the people

kidsContent.text: 6.  Do not kill.  —  God is the One who gives life, so no person should take another's life.
7.  Do not commit adultery.  —  A husband and wife belong only to each other and stay faithful.
8.  Do not steal.  —  Never take what isn't yours. God gives us all we need, so there's no reason to steal.
9.  Do not give false testimony.  —  Don't lie about others or spread unkind, untrue things — love your neighbor instead.
10.  Do not covet.  —  Don't be jealous of what others have; envy is like stealing in your heart. Trust God to give you what you need!
🌟 The last five commandments show us how to love the people around us — that's how God's people live!

lesson.practicePoint: This week, pick ONE of the last five commandments you find hard, and practice it on purpose — no unkind or untrue words, nothing taken, no jealousy. Come share how it went next week!

memoryVerse.text: Therefore you shall keep My commandments and do them; I am Jehovah.
memoryVerse.application: God doesn't just want us to KNOW His commandments — He wants us to DO them. When we obey His words, we grow into His proper people who look more like Him.

activity.title: ⚖️ Proper Person Challenge — Right or Wrong?

parts.text: Materials: Scenario cards, a GREEN 'God's way' sign and a RED 'Not God's way' sign, the five commandment cards (6–10)
Setup: Post commandments 6–10 on the wall. Put the GREEN sign on one side of the room and the RED sign on the other.
Round 1 — Right or Wrong?: The leader reads a real-life scenario (e.g. 'You find $5 on the floor at school and quietly keep it'). Kids run to GREEN or RED and name which commandment it matches.
Round 2 — Fix It: For each 'wrong' scenario, kids act out the RIGHT thing a proper person would do instead.
Round 3 — Heart Check: For coveting (#10), each kid names ONE thing they're thankful for instead of being jealous.
📖 Connection: God's commandments teach us to love the people around us — keeping them is how God's people live!

rolePlayScript.text: Scene: A school hallway. A group of friends is whispering. A new girl stands alone nearby.
One day at school, one of the girls started saying things about another girl — things that were not very nice, and not even true.
Did you hear about the new girl? I heard she did something really embarrassing. Pass it on!
Really? I'll tell everyone! This is such good gossip.
I don't really know her… but everyone's saying it, so I'll say it too, I guess.
The rumor spreads around the whole school. Later, 'Me' actually talks to the new girl.
Everyone keeps whispering about me… but none of it is true. It was just a misunderstanding. It really hurts.
Oh no. I repeated it without even knowing if it was true. I broke the ninth commandment — I gave false testimony against my neighbor.
God tells us not to give false testimony against our neighbor — and our neighbor is ANYONE around us: classmates, friends, even our brothers and sisters.
I'm so sorry. I'm going to tell everyone the truth and stop the rumor. God wants me to love my neighbor, not hurt her.
Thank you. That means so much to me.
God's people keep His commandments and DO them — we speak the truth and love our neighbor!

description.text: Setup: Two teams. At the far end, scatter cards — some describe keeping a commandment (6–10), some describe breaking one.
Rules: One runner at a time races down, grabs ONE card, reads it, and drops it in the 'KEEP IT' or 'BREAK IT' bucket back at base.
Scoring: Each correctly sorted card = 1 point. Wrong bucket = no point.
Bonus: For a 'KEEP IT' card, the runner shouts which commandment number (6–10) it matches for a bonus point.
📖 Connection: A proper person can tell right from wrong — and chooses to DO what God says!
Materials: Scenario cards, two buckets/boxes, cones

optionB.title: 🟢🔴 God's Way — Green Light, Red Light

description.text: Setup: Kids line up at one end; a leader stands at the far end as the 'caller.'

Rules: On 'GREEN — God's way!' the caller names a good action (tell the truth, share, honor parents) and kids move forward. On 'RED — not God's way!' the caller names a wrong action (lie, steal, be jealous) and everyone must FREEZE.
Out: Anyone who moves on a RED action goes back a few steps.
Winner: First to reach the caller and tag the wall wins and becomes the next caller.
📖 Connection: We 'go' toward what God commands and 'stop' what He says not to do — keeping His words!
Materials: Open space, optional green/red cards

movieViewing.title: Moses, God, and the Mountain
movieViewing.description: TBTMS story video — God gives His people the commandments at Mount Sinai (Exodus 19–20). A great recap as we finish all Ten Words.

description.text: Before kids arrive, hide 'treasures' (small tokens) around the area. Give each kid a color; they may only collect tokens of THEIR color.
Rule: If you find a token that isn't your color, leave it — practicing 'do not steal' and 'do not covet' what belongs to someone else.
Twist: At a whistle, everyone returns to base and shares one token they're thankful for (a thankful heart beats a jealous one!).
Finish: Count tokens together — everyone gets a treat, showing God provides for all of us.
Materials: Colored tokens or beads, small bags, a whistle

outdoor.tip: ⚖️ The last five commandments are all about loving the people around us. Help kids see that being honest, kind, and content is how God's people shine — obeying God's words in the small things too.
